edges.mechanism: Lipase inhibition reduces micellar uptake of fat-soluble hydrocarbon carotenoids; plasma lycopene fell then partly recovered over 4.5 months, while alpha- and beta-carotene fell 45% and 32%; orlistat cut beta-carotene absorption by about one-third.
edges.evidence: Small open study (n=6) plus a crossover PK study of beta-carotene; no lycopene PK study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Impaired intestinal absorption plus cholesterol lowering; cholestyramine lowered serum lycopene by 30% and beta-carotene by 40%.
edges.evidence: 3-year RCT in 303 hypercholesterolemic subjects; moderate certainty for the biomarker effect

edges.mechanism: Reduced lipoprotein particle size and competition for VLDL incorporation lowered serum carotenoids by 30-40%.
edges.evidence: 3-year RCT (n=303); drug rarely used

edges.mechanism: Statins lower LDL, the main carotenoid carrier, so crude plasma lycopene falls while lipid-adjusted lycopene rises or is unchanged; no loss of lycopene status.
edges.evidence: RCT of simvastatin 40 mg (n=80) and an 8-week cohort (n=76); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Ezetimibe inhibits SR-BI/NPC1L1-related transport; lycopene transport fell about 20% in Caco-2 cells.
edges.evidence: In vitro only; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Lycopene supplements lowered SBP by about 2-6 mmHg in some meta-analyses; this may add to antihypertensive drugs, but a 34-RCT GRADE meta-analysis found no BP effect.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs with conflicting results; no interaction study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: A water-soluble tomato extract (Fruitflow) inhibits platelet aggregation with about one-third of the effect of daily 75 mg aspirin and no significant additive effect; not demonstrated for lycopene itself.
edges.evidence: Crossover RCTs of tomato extract (n=47, n=90); relevant only to aqueous tomato-extract products; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Carotenoids compete for micellar incorporation and chylomicron secretion; co-ingesting lutein reduced the postprandial chylomicron response to lycopene, but 3-week plasma status was unaffected.
edges.evidence: Human crossover feeding study (n=20) plus review; low certainty; clinical impact likely negligible

edges.mechanism: Hydrocarbon carotenoids compete for absorption and lipoprotein exchange; high-dose beta-carotene also causes carotenodermia, additive with lycopenemia.
edges.evidence: Human feeding studies and review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Dietary fat improves lycopene micellarization and absorption; cooking tomatoes with olive oil raised plasma trans-lycopene 82%; unsaturated fats boost carotenoid bioavailability more than saturated fats.
edges.evidence: Small human feeding study plus MA of RCTs; moderate certainty for the bioavailability effect

edges.mechanism: Adding avocado (fat) to salsa increased lycopene absorption 4.4-fold; take supplements with a fat-containing meal.
edges.evidence: Crossover feeding studies and MA of RCTs; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: The non-absorbable fat substitute sequesters fat-soluble carotenoids; it lowered serum lycopene below the reference range, which a multivitamin did not prevent; customary use was linked to 4.3-22.4% lower carotenoids.
edges.evidence: 36-week controlled feeding study plus post-marketing surveillance (n=2535); moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Plant sterols reduce intestinal cholesterol and carotenoid uptake; serum lycopene fell 14.6% in adults with FH using sterol-ester spread.
edges.evidence: 26-week open-label follow-up (n=20 adults); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Combining lycopene (anti-proliferative) with curcumin (anti-inflammatory) synergistically attenuated testosterone-induced BPH in rats.
edges.evidence: Preclinical only (rat and cell models); very low certainty for humans

edges.mechanism: Lycopene 2 mg/d from 12-20 weeks did not prevent pre-eclampsia but was associated with more preterm labor (10.4% vs 1.2%) and low birthweight (22.1% vs 9.8%); an earlier RCT reported benefit; antioxidant MA showed no preventive benefit.
edges.evidence: Conflicting RCTs (n=159, n=251) and a MA of antioxidant RCTs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Tomato-derived oleoresin or extract products may carry tomato allergens; umbrella review flagged potential allergy.
edges.evidence: Umbrella review statement; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Lycopene may lower serum PSA in BPH or high-baseline-PSA patients; overall MAs show no effect and early falls may be transient and non-specific, so PSA trends during supplementation should be interpreted cautiously.
edges.evidence: Small RCTs plus two MAs of RCTs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Lycopene intake raises skin carotenoid reflection-spectroscopy scores used as fruit/vegetable intake biomarkers; genotype modifies the response.
edges.evidence: RCT (n=80) and case report; low certainty

edges.mechanism: EFSA based its 0.5 mg/kg bw/d ADI on a non-reversible ALT rise in a 1-year rat study; human carotenoid RCT meta-analysis found no ALT change.
edges.evidence: Animal toxicology plus GRADE MA of human RCTs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: BCO1 SNPs predicted plasma, prostate and skin lycopene/carotenoid responses; multi-SNP scores explain much of the inter-individual variability in absorption.
edges.evidence: Secondary analyses of small trials; not validated for dosing; low certainty
